title: Trace-class additivity for an arbitrary bounded filtered correspondence
statement:
Fix $A=A_{E,n}$ and separated finite-type $k$-schemes as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], and an admissible correspondence $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_kX$ of [def-trf-correspondence]. A bounded filtered derived object means a complex of $A$-module sheaves with a finite decreasing filtration by subcomplexes, localized at maps inducing quasi-isomorphisms on all graded complexes. Write $\omega$ for forgetting the filtration and $\operatorname{gr}^r$ for the associated graded complex. Require the underlying object and all graded pieces to be in $D^b_{ctf}$; the filtered six operations are the classical derived lifts on this localization. Let $\widetilde K$ be such an object on $X$ and let $\widetilde u:Rc_{1!}c_2^*\widetilde K\to\widetilde K$ be a morphism in this filtered derived category. Denote by $u$ and $u_r$ the exceptional adjoints of $\omega\widetilde u$ and $\operatorname{gr}^r\widetilde u$, respectively. Then the Verdier trace classes of [def-trf-trace-class] satisfy
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{c,\omega\widetilde K}(u)=\sum_r\operatorname{Tr}_{c,\operatorname{gr}^r\widetilde K}(u_r)\quad\text{in }\operatorname{Hom}_{D(F,A)}(A_F,\omega_{F,A}),\qquad F=\operatorname{Fix}(c).$$
The sum is finite. This assertion concerns a morphism in the filtered derived category; a mere morphism of distinguished triangles with commuting squares is not the hypothesis.

The filtered construction is on the small etale sites, with its finite filtered bounded-constructible objects and operations transported to the small pro-etale categories by the exact comparison of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. All displayed trace classes are read in the coefficient categories of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions].

source.place: §§5.1--5.2 (classical filtered derived category and six operations), Lemma 5.3.2

proof.text: Use the small etale filtered construction and its transport to the pro-etale coefficient categories specified in the statement. The finite filtered etale/pro-etale comparison, including compatibility with operations and trace transformations, is the last paragraph of [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom]. The ordinary bounded constructible comparison is [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]; no arbitrary filtered enhancement of a triangulated equivalence is inferred. The finite-stage six-functor and duality domains are those of [prop-functor-package], so the auxiliary structure, diagonal, projection and fixed-square operations used to define the trace class are available. Put $G=Rc_{1!}c_2^*$, $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$, $d:F\to X$, $K_r=\operatorname{gr}^r\widetilde K$ and $N=R\Gamma(F,\omega_{F,A})$, with $N$ concentrated in filtration degree zero. The filtered duality calculus [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom] makes $G\widetilde K$ an object of the same filtered constructible domain, with underlying $G\omega\widetilde K$ and graded pieces $GK_r$. In this proof $H$ and $N$ are complexes of abelian groups, not internal sheaf Hom objects. Filtered derived global sections on a scheme $T$ mean the global filtered Hom $R\operatorname{Hom}^F_T(A_T,-)$ from the coefficient unit in filtration degree zero, as supplied by [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom]. Its graded comparison is the one-variable case of that node's global Hom formula.

source.place: §§5.2.1--5.2.2 and §5.3.1 (with the two legs interchanged to match this project)

proof.text:
Set $H=R\operatorname{Hom}^F_X(G\widetilde K,\widetilde K)$, the global filtered Hom complex in $DF(\mathbf{Ab})$. We construct a filtered map $\widetilde\tau':H\to N$ by working with global derived Hom throughout. For ordinary independent inputs $P,Q\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ put $B=Q\boxtimes D_XP$. Exceptional adjunction gives
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_X(GP,Q)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_C(c_2^*P,c_1^!Q).$$
The exceptional internal-Hom exchange of [lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange], applied to the total map $c$ and $(p_2^*P,p_1^!Q)$, followed by the inverse of [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier] at $(M,N)=(Q,P)$, gives
$$R\mathcal Hom(c_2^*P,c_1^!Q)\simeq Rc^!R\mathcal Hom(p_2^*P,p_1^!Q)\simeq Rc^!B.$$
The composition comparisons identify $c^*p_2^*=c_2^*$ and $c^!p_1^!=c_1^!$. Apply derived global sections to this comparison. Next use the ordinary-adjunction unit $B\to R\Delta_*L\Delta^*B$ and the fixed-square base-change comparison of [lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality]. The result is the pre-evaluation map
$$T''_{P,Q}:R\operatorname{Hom}_X(GP,Q)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(F,Rd^!(D_XP\otimes^LQ)).$$
Indeed the intermediate target is $R\Gamma(C,Rc^!R\Delta_*L\Delta^*B)$; fixed-square base change identifies it with $R\Gamma(F,Rd^!L\Delta^*B)$, and diagonal pullback and signed tensor symmetry identify $L\Delta^*B=Q\otimes^LD_XP$ with $D_XP\otimes^LQ$. All these arrows are natural separately in the contravariant variable $P$ and the covariant variable $Q$, because the cited external-Hom and exceptional-exchange comparisons are natural in both variables. They have compatible filtered lifts by [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom]; filtered global sections are as defined in Step 1. The filtered lift of the Künneth comparison is invertible, so its inverse used above exists in the filtered category: by the same node its graded maps are direct sums of ordinary Künneth comparisons, hence isomorphisms, so its cone has zero graded pieces and is zero, the graded pieces jointly detecting zero objects. On setting both variables to $\widetilde K$, compose the filtered $T''$ with $R\Gamma^F(F,Rd^!(-))$ of evaluation and $Rd^!\omega_X\simeq\omega_{F,A}$ to obtain $\widetilde\tau'$. On forgetting the filtration and applying exceptional adjunction, this is exactly the global trace-map composite of [lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality]. Indeed at $P=Q=K$ the composite of the compositors, the exchange and $Rc^!$ of the inverse Künneth comparison is the external-duality comparison $\xi:\mathcal H_c(K)\simeq Rc^!(K\boxtimes^L_AD_XK)$ of [thm-trf-verdier-duality] that the trace map uses, with the external product in the same order; and the rearrangement of unit, fixed-square base change and $e'$ is naturality of base change, since $e_K=R\Delta_*(e')\circ(\text{unit})$. In that composite its $e_K$ is the ordinary-adjunction transpose of diagonal evaluation. Thus [def-trf-trace-class] identifies its value on $\omega\widetilde u$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_{c,\omega\widetilde K}(u)$. Every construction here uses the constructible domains checked in Step 1, including the total map $c$, both projections and the structure maps; no sheafified adjunction is being deduced merely from an abstract triangulated Hom bijection.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.2 proof, construction of Tr′ and factorization through Tr″ followed by evaluation

proof.text:
By the global Hom statement of [lem-trf-filtered-derived-hom-calculus],
$$\operatorname{gr}^0H\simeq\bigoplus_r R\operatorname{Hom}_X(GK_r,K_r).$$
Apply the graded-transformation compatibility of [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom] to the pre-evaluation transformation $T''$ of Step 2, using its bifiltered tensor/internal-Hom formulas and global Hom formula. The first variable is contravariant: its degree $r$ contributes dual filtration degree $-r$. Thus total degree zero pairs exactly equal input indices. The resulting degree-zero transformation is the direct sum of the ordinary maps
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_X(GK_r,K_r)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(F,Rd^!(D_XK_r\otimes^LK_r)).$$
The compatibility clause identifies the arrows themselves, not just their source and target objects.

Check evaluation separately, since it is not a transformation in two independent copies of $K$. The convention of [def-trf-dualizing-complex] makes evaluation $D_X^F\widetilde K\otimes^L\widetilde K\to\omega_X$ the transpose of $1_{D_X^F\widetilde K}$ under the filtered tensor--Hom adjunction of [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom]. The duality index formula, obtained by setting the second internal-Hom variable equal to $\omega_X$ in filtration degree zero, gives $\operatorname{gr}^{-r}D_X^F\widetilde K\simeq D_XK_r$. The global morphism-projection clause of [lem-trf-filtered-derived-hom-calculus] sends that identity to the identities of these graded duals. Compatibility of the adjunction and evaluation with the graded comparisons, in [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom], therefore identifies evaluation on the summand $D_XK_r\otimes^LK_r$ with the ordinary evaluation of $K_r$. The signed symmetry in Step 2 is the same ordinary derived symmetry on that summand. Composing with Step 3, the restriction of $\operatorname{gr}^0\widetilde\tau'$ to $R\operatorname{Hom}_X(GK_r,K_r)$ is the ordinary trace map $\tau'_{K_r}$. There is no factor $(-1)^r$, since $r$ is a filtration index and carries no cochain shift.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.2 proof, evaluation compatibility from gr^i(Id)=Id

proof.text:
The global Hom identification in [lem-trf-filtered-derived-hom-calculus] represents $\widetilde u$ by $[\widetilde u]\in H^0(\omega t^{\geq0}H)$. Its image in $H^0(\omega H)$ is the underlying map. Since $N=R\Gamma(F,\omega_{F,A})$ is in filtration degree zero, $t^{\geq0}N=N=t^{\leq0}N$. Apply first $t^{\geq0}$ and then the natural quotient to $t^{\leq0}$ to $\widetilde\tau'$. Naturality of this quotient gives the factorization
$$\omega t^{\geq0}H\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}^0H\xrightarrow{\operatorname{gr}^0\widetilde\tau'}N.$$
Here $t^{\leq0}t^{\geq0}H$ is the degree-zero filtered object associated to $\operatorname{gr}^0H$, so this is an equality of maps in the localized category, using its actual truncation functors. The same Hom lemma sends $[\widetilde u]$ under the projection to the tuple $(\operatorname{gr}^r\widetilde u)_r$. Step 4 therefore evaluates its image as $\sum_r\tau'_{K_r}(\operatorname{gr}^r\widetilde u)$. By [def-trf-trace-class] and exceptional adjunction these summands are $\operatorname{Tr}_{c,K_r}(u_r)$, while the original image is $\operatorname{Tr}_{c,\omega\widetilde K}(u)$. This gives the desired identity in $H^0(F,\omega_{F,A})=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(F,A)}(A_F,\omega_{F,A})$. Only finitely many $K_r$ are nonzero. The last paragraph of [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom] identifies both the filtered objects and these trace-construction transformations under the finite-coefficient etale/pro-etale comparison, giving the displayed identity in the specified pro-etale category. At no point was the coefficient morphism inverted.
